source: MAFF Cashew Farmer Guide -- Harvest and Post-Harvest Handling
text: Cashew harvest season runs roughly from February to April/May. When picking fruit for local sale, avoid bruising it during harvest. It is generally better to let fruit ripen and drop naturally for the best-quality harvest, especially for export-quality product. For fallen ripe fruit collected from the ground: separate the cashew apple (fruit flesh) from the nut, wash the nuts clean, sun-dry for 2-3 days, then pack into sacks and store in a dry warehouse. If selling fresh/wet cashew nuts rather than dried ones, farmers can simply separate the nut from the fruit flesh and sell by weight immediately without drying.
